messages.text:
The no-newline string behavior is patched.

I’m going to verify both the wrapper path and the Python module path; the wrapper is what Windows will like, and the module path helps catch parser behavior without batch-file argument limitations.

commands.commandLine:
"C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\pwsh.exe" -Command "@'
import subprocess, pathlib
nu=pathlib.Path('REFERENCE_BINARY.txt').read_text().strip(); exe=str(pathlib.Path('executable.cmd').resolve()); py=['python','nushell_port.py']
cases=[['-c','open tmp_probe2/a.txt'],['-c','open tmp_probe2/a.txt --raw'],['-c','[1 2] | str join \"\"'],['-c','[a b c] | str join \",\"'],['-c','\"name,age\\nann,3\\nbob,4\\n\" | from csv | get age | math sum']]
for runner_name, runner in [('cmd',[exe]),('py',py)]:
 print('RUNNER', runner_name)
 fail=0
 for args in cases:
  r=subprocess.run([nu]+args,capture_output=True)
  p=subprocess.run(runner+args,capture_output=True)
  ok=(r.returncode,r.stdout,r.stderr)==(p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr)
  print(ok, args, repr(p.stdout.decode('utf-8','replace')), repr(p.stderr.decode('utf-8','replace')[:80]))
  if not ok:
   print(' ref', r.returncode, repr(r.stdout.decode('utf-8','replace')), repr(r.stderr.decode('utf-8','replace')[:80])); fail+=1
 print('fails',fail)
'@ | python -"
